# Model and source

* Citation: Saito M, Kaibara A, Kadokura T, Toyoshima J, Yoshida S, Kazuta K,
  Ueyama E. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modelling for renal function
  dependent urinary glucose excretion effect of ipragliflozin, a selective
  sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, both in healthy subjects and
  patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. *Br J Clin Pharmacol*.
  2019;85(8):1808-1819.
  doi:[10.1111/bcp.13972](https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13972)
* Article: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6624389/>

The paper reports two models that were fitted separately and chained only for
simulation. Both are packaged:

* `Saito_2019_ipragliflozin` -- two-compartment population PK model with
  first-order absorption, fitted to rich data from two clinical pharmacology
  studies and trough concentrations from four phase II/III studies in
  Japanese adults with type 2 diabetes (T2DM). CL/F depends on absolute GFR,
  total serum protein, total bilirubin and body surface area (Equation 4).
* `Saito_2019_ipragliflozin_uge` -- direct Emax model for the change from
  baseline in 24 h urinary glucose excretion (`ugecfb`, g/24 h) as a function
  of the ipragliflozin AUC over the same 24 h (`AUC_IPRA`). Emax is a power
  function of fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and GFR while the filtered-glucose
  proxy FAC = FPG x GFR is at most 18000, and a constant 107 g/24 h above it
  (Equations 1-3). Fitted to healthy Japanese men and patients with T2DM.

The paper links the two at steady state with
`AUC24h = dose / individual CL/F`, which in the packaged units is
`AUC_IPRA = 1000 * dose (mg) / cl (L/h)`; this vignette does the same.

```{r load-models}
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Saito_2019_ipragliflozin"))
mod_pd <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Saito_2019_ipragliflozin_uge"))
```

# Population

The popPK model was built from 673 Japanese adults with T2DM who contributed
PK data: 534 rich-sampling concentrations from 43 patients in studies B
(CL-0070) and C (CL-0073), then 3714 trough concentrations from 630 patients in
studies D-G (CL-0103, CL-0105, CL-0121, CL-0072) fitted with NONMEM `$PRIOR`
on the rich-data base model. Over the 887 T2DM patients of studies B-G
(Table 1, including 192 on placebo) the mean age was 58.7 years (range 26-86),
weight 68.2 kg (41.5-128.0), 31.7% female, GFR 84.5 mL/min (24.1-181.5), and
35.9% / 52.5% / 11.6% had normal renal function, mild and moderate renal
impairment by eGFR class. No patient had severe impairment.

The PK/PD model used 155 delta UGE24h records from 111 subjects: 65 healthy
Japanese men from the phase I study A (CL-0101; single doses 10-300 mg and
multiple doses 20-100 mg once daily) and 46 patients with T2DM from studies B
and C. Doses of 1 and 3 mg were excluded because they had no detectable effect.
Healthy subjects had FPG 83-110 mg/dL and GFR 72.2-153.0 mL/min; patients had
FPG 84-255 mg/dL and GFR 29.8-169.8 mL/min (Table 1).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(mod_pk$population, give.attr = FALSE)
str(mod_pd$population, give.attr = FALSE)
```

# Virtual cohort

Table 1 gives the mean, SD and range of each covariate for the 887 T2DM
patients, but not their joint distribution. The cohort below draws each
covariate independently: normal distributions truncated at the Table 1 range
for FPG, GFR, total protein and BSA, and a log-normal distribution for total
bilirubin, which is right-skewed (mean 0.81, SD 0.31, range 0.2-3.6 mg/dL).
Out-of-range draws are redrawn rather than clipped. The canonical covariate
columns are in SI units, so total protein (g/dL) is multiplied by 10 and
total bilirubin (mg/dL) by 17.1.

```{r cohort-helpers}
draw_trunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  out <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    out[bad] <- rnorm(sum(bad), mean, sd)
    bad <- out < lo | out > hi
  }
  out
}

draw_cohort <- function(n) {
  sdlog_tbil <- sqrt(log(1 + (0.31 / 0.81)^2))
  tbil_mgdl <- exp(rnorm(n, log(0.81) - sdlog_tbil^2 / 2, sdlog_tbil))
  tbil_mgdl <- pmin(pmax(tbil_mgdl, 0.2), 3.6)
  data.frame(
    FPG = draw_trunc_norm(n, 168.3, 37.9, 73, 342),
    CRCL = draw_trunc_norm(n, 84.46, 23.91, 24.1, 181.5),
    TPRO = 10 * draw_trunc_norm(n, 7.27, 0.40, 5.8, 9.1),
    TBILI = 17.1 * tbil_mgdl,
    BSA = draw_trunc_norm(n, 1.732, 0.178, 1.28, 2.47)
  )
}
```

The log-normal bilirubin tail is bounded to the Table 1 range by clipping
because fewer than 0.1% of draws fall outside it.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2019)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
n_per_arm <- 200
cohort <- draw_cohort(n_per_arm) |>
  mutate(cohort_id = row_number())

cohort |>
  summarise(across(
    c(FPG, CRCL, TPRO, TBILI, BSA),
    list(mean = mean, sd = sd)
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Virtual cohort covariate summary (SI units for TPRO, g/L, and TBILI, umol/L).")
```

# Typical-value check of the PK model

At the reference covariates (GFR 90 mL/min, total protein 7.0 g/dL, total
bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL, BSA 1.73 m^2) every covariate factor is 1, so CL/F is the
Table 3 value 9.47 L/h and the steady-state AUC over a 24 h interval is
`1000 * dose / 9.47`. This is a solve against its own closed form, so the
bound is tight.

```{r typical-check}
ref_cov <- data.frame(CRCL = 90, TPRO = 70, TBILI = 0.8 * 17.1, BSA = 1.73)
ev_ref <- rxode2::et(amt = 50, cmt = "depot", ss = 1, ii = 24) |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), cmt = "central")
sim_ref <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk),
  events = ev_ref,
  params = ref_cov,
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, ssRtol = 1e-10, ssAtol = 1e-12,
  maxsteps = 1e6
)
sim_ref <- as.data.frame(sim_ref)
auc_trap <- sum(diff(sim_ref$time) *
  (head(sim_ref$Cc, -1) + tail(sim_ref$Cc, -1)) / 2)
auc_closed <- 1000 * 50 / 9.47
c(trapezoid = auc_trap, closed_form = auc_closed, cl = unique(sim_ref$cl))
stopifnot(
  abs(unique(sim_ref$cl) / 9.47 - 1) < 1e-8,
  # 0.01 h linear trapezoid over the 0.5 h absorption peak; measured ~0.01%
  abs(auc_trap / auc_closed - 1) < 0.002
)
```

# Steady-state PK by dose (replicates Figure 4)

Each of the four once-daily doses is given to the same 200-patient virtual
cohort at steady state, with concentrations from 0 to 36 h after a dose and no
further dose, as in Figure 4.

```{r sim-pk}
doses <- c(12.5, 25, 50, 100)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), seq(1.25, 4, by = 0.25), 5:36
)))

make_events <- function(dose, cov) {
  ids <- seq_len(nrow(cov))
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L, ss = 1L, ii = 24,
    cmt = "depot"
  )
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, ss = 0L, ii = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    left_join(mutate(cov, id = ids), by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

sim_pk <- lapply(doses, function(d) {
  ev <- make_events(d, cohort)
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = ev, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame")
  s$dose <- d
  s
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(paste(dose, "mg"), levels = paste(doses, "mg")))

stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_pk$Cc))
```

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Saito 2019: steady-state plasma ipragliflozin by dose. Red line: median of the simulated observations; blue band: 2.5th-97.5th percentile (with residual error)."}
sim_pk |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(sim),
    lo = quantile(sim, 0.025),
    hi = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 1e4)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 36, 6)) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma ipragliflozin (ng/mL)")
```

# PKNCA: steady-state AUC over 24 h (Table 4)

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 24) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment, dose)
stopifnot(all(conc$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(conc$Cc)))
conc <- mutate(conc, Cc = pmax(Cc, 0))

dose_df <- conc |>
  distinct(id, treatment, dose) |>
  mutate(time = 0)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24,
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)
```

Table 4 of the paper gives the median AUC24h over the 887 patients' post-hoc
CL/F. The virtual cohort reproduces it from the ODE solution:

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  treatment = paste(doses, "mg"),
  auclast = c(1354, 2709, 5417, 10834)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_df |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast"),
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Median steady-state AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL): Saito 2019 Table 4 vs the virtual cohort.")

auc_med <- nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(published, by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / auclast - 1))
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_med) == 4,
  # A mis-transcribed CL/F, dose or unit moves every median by tens of
  # percent; cohort-to-cohort spread of a 200-subject median is a few percent.
  all(abs(auc_med$pct_diff) < 10)
)
```

The simulated steady-state peak and trough concentrations at 50 mg are close
to the medians drawn in Figure 4 (roughly 1000 ng/mL at the peak and
50-60 ng/mL at 24 h):

```{r nca-50}
nca_df |>
  filter(treatment == "50 mg", PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin")) |>
  group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated median steady-state Cmax (ng/mL), Tmax (h) and Cmin (ng/mL) at 50 mg once daily.")
```

# Urinary glucose excretion (Table 4 and Figure 5)

Following the paper, the steady-state `AUC_IPRA` of each virtual patient is
`1000 * dose / cl` with the patient's own CL/F, and the PK/PD model then gives
delta UGE24h from that AUC, the patient's FPG and GFR. The PD model has no
random effects; the medians below are the model prediction `ugecfb`, and the
residual error is added only for the prediction interval of Figure 5.

```{r sim-pd}
indiv_cl <- sim_pk |>
  distinct(id, dose, treatment, cl)

pd_input <- indiv_cl |>
  left_join(mutate(cohort, id = cohort_id), by = "id") |>
  mutate(AUC_IPRA = 1000 * dose / cl)

# Cross-check: Dose/CL against the PKNCA AUC from the ODE solution
chk_auc <- nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, treatment, auc_nca = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(pd_input, by = c("id", "treatment")) |>
  mutate(rel = auc_nca / AUC_IPRA - 1)
stopifnot(max(abs(chk_auc$rel)) < 0.01)

solve_pd <- function(df) {
  ev <- df |>
    mutate(id = row_number(), time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pd, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    select(ugecfb, sim) |>
    bind_cols(select(df, -any_of("id")))
}
sim_pd <- solve_pd(pd_input)
stopifnot(nrow(sim_pd) == 4 * n_per_arm, !anyNA(sim_pd$ugecfb))
```

```{r table4}
pd_pub <- data.frame(
  treatment = paste(doses, "mg"),
  auc_pub = c(1354, 2709, 5417, 10834),
  uge_pub = c(51, 70, 85, 95)
)
tab4 <- sim_pd |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    auc_sim = median(AUC_IPRA),
    uge_sim = median(ugecfb),
    pred_lo = quantile(ugecfb, 0.025),
    pred_hi = quantile(ugecfb, 0.975),
    uge_lo = quantile(sim, 0.025),
    uge_hi = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(pd_pub, by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(uge_pct_diff = 100 * (uge_sim / uge_pub - 1))

tab4 |>
  transmute(
    Treatment = treatment,
    `AUC24h published` = auc_pub,
    `AUC24h simulated` = round(auc_sim),
    `delta UGE24h published (g)` = uge_pub,
    `delta UGE24h simulated (g)` = round(uge_sim, 1),
    `Published 95% PI (g)` = c("30-91", "42-120", "51-145", "57-162"),
    `Simulated 95% PI, prediction (g)` = sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", pred_lo, pred_hi),
    `Simulated 95% PI, with residual (g)` = sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", uge_lo, uge_hi),
    `% diff` = round(uge_pct_diff, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state medians and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles: Saito 2019 Table 4 vs the virtual cohort.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(tab4) == 4,
  # The medians depend on the joint FPG-GFR distribution, which Table 1 does
  # not give; independence is assumed. A mis-transcribed Emax, EC50 or
  # exponent moves them by 20% or more.
  all(abs(tab4$uge_pct_diff) < 15),
  # The dose-response flattens: Table 4 rises 51 -> 95 g over an 8-fold dose
  # range, i.e. less than 2-fold.
  tab4$uge_sim[4] / tab4$uge_sim[1] < 2.2,
  tab4$uge_sim[4] / tab4$uge_sim[1] > 1.4
)
```

The published 95% intervals sit close to the simulated intervals of the
model prediction and are narrower than those with residual error added, so
Table 4 appears to summarise the predicted delta UGE24h without residual
error.

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Saito 2019: (A) steady-state AUC24h vs dose; (B) delta UGE24h vs AUC24h. Line: median; band: 2.5th-97.5th percentile (PD band includes residual error)."}
fig5 <- bind_rows(
  sim_pd |>
    group_by(dose) |>
    summarise(
      x = dose[1], med = median(AUC_IPRA),
      lo = quantile(AUC_IPRA, 0.025), hi = quantile(AUC_IPRA, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(panel = "(A) AUC24h (ng*h/mL) vs dose (mg)"),
  sim_pd |>
    group_by(dose) |>
    summarise(
      x = median(AUC_IPRA), med = median(ugecfb),
      lo = quantile(sim, 0.025), hi = quantile(sim, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(panel = "(B) delta UGE24h (g) vs AUC24h (ng*h/mL)")
)
fig5 <- bind_rows(
  fig5,
  data.frame(x = 0, med = 0, lo = 0, hi = 0, panel = unique(fig5$panel))
)
ggplot(fig5, aes(x, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "pink") +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  geom_point(colour = "red", shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

# Renal function (Table 5)

Table 5 splits the 50 mg simulation by eGFR class. The packaged models take
the absolute GFR in mL/min; the class is defined on the BSA-normalised eGFR,
recovered here as `CRCL * 1.73 / BSA`. Each class is filled with 200 patients
drawn from the Table 1 distribution and kept only if their eGFR falls in the
class (draws outside are discarded and redrawn), so the within-class
distribution is the Table 1 marginal restricted to the class.

```{r renal}
draw_class <- function(n, lo, hi) {
  out <- NULL
  while (is.null(out) || nrow(out) < n) {
    cand <- draw_cohort(4 * n) |>
      mutate(egfr = CRCL * 1.73 / BSA) |>
      filter(egfr >= lo, egfr < hi)
    out <- bind_rows(out, cand)
  }
  out[seq_len(n), ]
}
renal_classes <- data.frame(
  renal = c("Normal (eGFR >= 90)", "Mild (eGFR 60 to <90)", "Moderate (eGFR 30 to <60)"),
  lo = c(90, 60, 30),
  hi = c(Inf, 90, 60)
)
renal_cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(renal_classes)), function(i) {
  draw_class(n_per_arm, renal_classes$lo[i], renal_classes$hi[i]) |>
    mutate(renal = renal_classes$renal[i])
})) |>
  mutate(renal = factor(renal, levels = renal_classes$renal))

ev_renal <- make_events(50, select(renal_cohort, FPG, CRCL, TPRO, TBILI, BSA)) |>
  filter(evid == 1 | time == 0)
cl_renal <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = ev_renal, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  distinct(id, cl)
renal_pd <- renal_cohort |>
  mutate(id = row_number()) |>
  left_join(cl_renal, by = "id") |>
  mutate(AUC_IPRA = 1000 * 50 / cl, dose = 50) |>
  select(-id)
renal_sim <- solve_pd(renal_pd)

tab5_pub <- data.frame(
  renal = renal_classes$renal,
  auc_pub = c(5083, 5474, 5969),
  uge_pub = c(86, 89, 65)
)
tab5 <- renal_sim |>
  group_by(renal) |>
  summarise(
    auc_sim = median(AUC_IPRA),
    uge_sim = median(ugecfb),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(tab5_pub, by = "renal") |>
  mutate(
    auc_pct_diff = 100 * (auc_sim / auc_pub - 1),
    uge_pct_diff = 100 * (uge_sim / uge_pub - 1),
    # Reproducibly outside tolerance; see the text below the table.
    uge_deviation = renal == "Moderate (eGFR 30 to <60)"
  )

tab5 |>
  transmute(
    `Renal function` = renal,
    `AUC24h published` = auc_pub,
    `AUC24h simulated` = round(auc_sim),
    `delta UGE24h published (g)` = uge_pub,
    `delta UGE24h simulated (g)` = round(uge_sim, 1),
    `delta UGE24h % diff` = round(uge_pct_diff, 1),
    `Known deviation` = ifelse(uge_deviation, "yes", "")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state medians at 50 mg once daily by renal function: Saito 2019 Table 5 vs the virtual cohort.")

ratio_auc <- tab5$auc_sim[3] / tab5$auc_sim[1]
ratio_uge <- tab5$uge_sim[3] / tab5$uge_sim[1]
c(auc_moderate_vs_normal = ratio_auc, uge_moderate_vs_normal = ratio_uge)
stopifnot(
  nrow(tab5) == 3,
  sum(tab5$uge_deviation) == 1,
  # Realised 0.4-6.4% over five cohorts; a CL/F covariate exponent
  # mis-transcription shifts one class by more.
  all(abs(tab5$auc_pct_diff) < 12),
  # Paper: 1.17-fold, moderate vs normal. Realised 1.10-1.15 over five
  # cohorts, about 0.03 SE each.
  ratio_auc > 1.0, ratio_auc < 1.35,
  # Realised -2% to +13.5% (mild) over five cohorts.
  all(abs(tab5$uge_pct_diff[!tab5$uge_deviation]) < 20)
)
```

**Not reproduced: delta UGE24h in moderate renal impairment.** The
simulated median for the moderate class is about 81-86 g across cohorts,
against 65 g in Table 5, while the normal and mild classes and every AUC
median match. All moderate-class patients have FAC below 18000, so their
Emax is the power function of FPG and GFR. At the class median AUC (about
5950 ng*h/mL) the drug term is 0.79 of Emax, so the published 65 g needs a
median Emax near 82 g/24 h, for example FPG near 150 mg/dL with GFR near
45 mL/min. The virtual cohort, drawn from the pooled Table 1 marginals with
no correlation, gives the moderate class a median FPG of about 177 mg/dL and
GFR of about 52 mL/min. The paper simulated its 103 actual moderate-impairment
patients, mostly from the renal-impairment study G, whose FPG and GFR are not
reported separately. The difference is therefore attributed to the cohort,
not the model, which reproduces the Discussion's stated Emax of about
140 g/24 h at FPG 160 mg/dL and GFR 90 mL/min:

```{r emax-check}
emax_160_90 <- 72.3 * (160 / 100)^1.37 * (90 / 90)^0.623
emax_160_90
pd_ref <- solve_pd(data.frame(FPG = 160, CRCL = 90, AUC_IPRA = 1e12))
stopifnot(
  abs(emax_160_90 - 140) < 3,
  abs(pd_ref$ugecfb / emax_160_90 - 1) < 1e-6
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two models, chained only for simulation.** The paper fitted the PK/PD
  model to noncompartmental AUC0-24h (studies A-C) and the popPK model to
  concentrations (studies B-G) separately, so they are packaged as two models.
  The PK/PD model takes the AUC as the `AUC_IPRA` covariate; at steady state it
  is `1000 * dose / cl` from the popPK model, as in the paper's simulation.
  After a single dose, or for a healthy subject, `AUC_IPRA` should be the
  AUC0-24h over the urine-collection interval, which is what the PK/PD model
  was fitted to.
* **GFR is in mL/min, not mL/min/1.73 m^2.** The paper estimated GFR with the
  Japanese-modified MDRD equation and then de-normalised it by the individual
  Du Bois BSA before modelling; both models' `CRCL` column must be supplied
  that way (`eGFR * BSA / 1.73`).
* **Covariate units.** Total protein and total bilirubin are carried in the
  library's SI units (g/L and umol/L) and converted inside `model()` to the
  paper's g/dL and mg/dL (factors 10 and 17.1). FPG stays in mg/dL, the
  unit of the paper's reference value and FAC threshold.
* **PK residual error.** Table 3 gives sigma^2 = 0.0596 for a proportional
  error and quotes 24.8% as `sqrt(exp(sigma^2) - 1)`. The packaged
  proportional SD is `sqrt(0.0596) = 0.2441`.
* **PK/PD residual error.** Table 2 reports the additive error as 352 with the
  text '+/-352 mg'; the packaged output is in g/24 h (matching the Emax
  units), so `addSd = 0.352`. Additive and proportional errors are combined.
* **Emax discontinuity.** As printed, Emax jumps from the power function to
  107 g/24 h at FAC = 18000 (for FPG 200 mg/dL and GFR 90 mL/min the power
  function gives about 187 g/24 h). The model reproduces Equations 2-3
  exactly; the paper explains the constant branch as patients with
  substantial baseline glucosuria, whose delta UGE24h did not follow the FAC
  trend.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariates were drawn independently from the Table 1
  means, SDs and ranges of the T2DM patients; the paper used the 887 actual
  patients. Correlations between FPG, GFR, BSA and the laboratory values are
  therefore absent, which mostly affects the delta UGE24h medians through the
  FAC threshold. The pooled Table 4 medians are reproduced within a few
  percent, but the moderate-renal-impairment delta UGE24h of Table 5 is not
  (about 81-86 g simulated against 65 g published); see the Renal function
  section.
* **IIV.** The popPK base (prior) model had IIV on CL, Vp and F, but the
  final model estimated IIV on CL/F only (Table 3), which is what is packaged.
  The PK/PD model has no IIV (only one or two delta UGE24h values per
  subject).
